Hmmmm. I see what you mean. When I think about it the reason I liked that format it was because I was rewatching it after I had seen the newer episodes. There are so many clues and such in the old episodes that you really start to appreciate when you see the newer ones.  For example, you can see an accessory in an early episode, but you wouldn't understand its significance until a later episode. A plot device in an early episode is used to blow up a major structure in a later episode. Or the murals we see in an early episode that become much more significant as the story goes on and we learn about the backstory. Basically, I like that there are a lot of seemingly trivial things we see in the background of the earlier episodes that turn out to be super important in the later episodes. I miss the feeling of revelation I guess.

People these days feel like it's the only solid conclusion to a characters is to kill them off. Personally I disagree, killing a character is usually lazy storytelling unless it has some significance to their character. Like a coward sacrificing himself to save his friends or a villain dying because they're arrogant.

I know what you mean, if you know none of the characters are in danger then what's the point? But what I'm saying is killing off a character to end their story is an increasingly common occurrence these days and a lot of the time it is a waste. Especially with villain characters. Too many stories end with "we murdered the big bad guy and his cronies, now everything is happy again." Look at how those animated series handle things. Those are great examples the main antagonists not just being killed off and often serving roles in later episodes. You have them join the good guys, being imprisoned and reflecting on their crimes, or just changing their ways and moving with their lives. To me it's just more compelling storytelling. The bad guys aren't necessarily just bad guys. They are people with different perspectives. Then again everyone I know says I have too much sympathy for villains. /shrug

Oh man, this reminds me of the time I was in school and an administrator accused me of being a potential threat because of an assignment for a writing class I left in another class. In writing class we were doing obituaries and could pick to do them on a classmate or a generic person we read a short story about. I chose a friend. I wrote it up and drew a little doodle of his funeral with like: RIP my friend written on it. I later went to some dumb one-time guest speaker presentation in another class and just continued to doodle the whole time. But when I left, I forgot my notebook with all of this in it on the table. Later in the day my friend gets called into the office because his name is in the notebook. Then I get called to the office when he tells them it's mine. The administrator proceeds to give me this big lecture on how everything in my notebook is unacceptable and is the EXACT SAME kind of stuff they found in the notebooks of past school shooters, specifically writing someone's obituary. I explain to her the stuff she is upset about was a class assignment and then she gets all confused and flustered before ordering me to never draw at school again. I'm like "Sure whatever, can I go now?" I told all my friends about it later and one of them who fancied them self a student activist told me that was bullshit and apparently went to her office to yell at her on my behalf, but I never heard anything else about it.
